layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The Segment Anything Model (SAM) represents a state-of-the-art research ad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vancement in natural image segmentation, achieving impressive results with input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompts such as points and bounding boxes. However, our evaluation and recent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: research indicate that directly applying the pretrained SAM to medical image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation does not yield satisfactory performance. This limitation primarily

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: arises from significant domain gap between natural images and medical images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To bridge this gap, we introduce SAM-Med2D, the most comprehensive studies on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applying SAM to medical 2D images. Its comprehensiveness manifests in three

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aspects: the comprehensive analysis on collecting the largest medical data, the most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comprehensive studies on various fine-tuning options, the most comprehensive eval-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uation on the performance. Specifically, we first collect and curate approximately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.6M images and 19.7M masks from public and private datasets, constructing a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large-scale medical image segmentation dataset encompassing various modalities

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and objects. Then, we comprehensively fine-tune SAM on this dataset and turn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it into SAM-Med2D. Unlike previous methods that only adopt bounding box or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: point prompts as interactive segmentation approach, we adapt SAM to medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image segmentation through more comprehensive prompts involving bounding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boxes, points, and masks. We additionally fine-tune the encoder and decoder of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the original SAM to obtain a well-performed SAM-Med2D, leading to the most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comprehensive fine-tuning strategies to date. Finally, we conducted a comprehen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sive evaluation and analysis to investigate the performance of SAM-Med2D in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image segmentation across various modalities, anatomical structures, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: organs. Concurrently, we validated the generalization capability of SAM-Med2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on 9 datasets from MICCAI 2023 challenge. Overall, our approach demonstrated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: significantly superior performance and generalization capability compared to SAM.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our codes can be found at https://github.com/uni-medical/SAM-Med2D.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in the analysis of medical images by identifying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and delineating various tissues, organs, or regions of interest. Accurate segmentation can assist

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: doctors in precisely identifying and locating areas of pathology, enabling more accurate diagnosis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and treatment [1]. Furthermore, quantitative and qualitative analysis of medical images provides

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comprehensive insights into the morphology, structure, and function of different tissues or organs,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: facilitating disease research and discoveries [2]. However, most existing methods are limited to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specific modalities, organs, or lesions due to the characteristics of medical imagery, such as numerous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This work is done when Junlong Cheng is an intern at Shanghai AI Laboratory.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modalities, complex tissue and organ structures, and few annotated data available [3, 4, 5]. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limitation hinders the generalizability and adaptability of algorithms, making it challenging to apply

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: them across diverse clinical scenarios.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 1: Comparison between examples in SA-1B (a) and in our dataset (b). SA-1B consists of 11M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: natural images and their corresponding 1129M masks. Our dataset consists of 4.6M medical images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and their corresponding 19.7M masks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recently, the trend towards large-scale models has created a buzz throughout the AI field. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: emergence of general-AI models such as ChatGPT2, ERNIE Bot 3, DINO [6], SegGPT [7], SAM [8],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: facilitates the use of a single model to address multiple tasks. As the latest large-scale vision model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM enables users to generate masks for specific regions of interest through interactive clicking,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bounding boxes, or providing natural language prompts. Its zero-shot and few-shot capabilities on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: natural images [9, 10] have garnered significant attention across various domains.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the field of medical imaging, some works [11, 12, 13, 14, 15] have also focused on the zero-shot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capabilities of SAMs. However, due to the significant domain gap between natural images and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical images, SAM struggles to generalize to multi-modal and multi-object medical datasets,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resulting in unstable segmentation performance across datasets. The reason can be attributed to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data collection methods: medical images are collected from certain protocols and scanners and are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presented as different modalities (electrons, lasers, X-rays, ultrasound, nuclear physics, and magnetic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resonance) due to their particular clinical purpose. As such, these images are based on a range of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: physics-based properties and energy sources, which differ greatly from natural images. As shown

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Figure 1, there are significant differences between natural images and medical images in terms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of pixel intensity, color, texture, and other distribution characteristics. Therefore, the limitation that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM cannot directly be applied to the medical domain is expected [11, 12, 13, 14, 15]: given that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM is trained on natural images only, it lacks specific knowledge related to medical imaging.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Equipping SAM with medical knowledge is hard because of the high annotation cost and the diverse

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotation quality. Preparing medical data requires domain knowledge and their quality varies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: significantly across hospitals and clinical studies. These challenges have resulted in a significant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: disparity between the quantities of medical images and natural images. The bar chart in Figure 1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compares the data volume of publicly available natural image datasets and medical image datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For instance, Totalsegmentor, the largest public segmentation dataset in the medical domain, also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has a significant gap compared to Open Image v6 [42] and SA-1B [8]. In this study, our objective is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to transfer SAM from natural images to medical images. This will provide benchmark models and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluation frameworks for researchers in medical image analysis to explore and enhance. To achieve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this goal, we proposed SAM-Med2D, the most comprehensive studies on applying SAM to medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2D images by addressing the following issues:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • How to fine-tune SAM for the medical imaging domain?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) We needed to incorporate knowledge about medical images into SAM, so we collected and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curated a medical image segmentation dataset comprising over 4.6M images and 19.7M masks. To

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the best of our knowledge, this dataset represents the largest medical image segmentation dataset,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encompassing multiple modalities and covering comprehensive objects. Table 1 illustrates the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods for fine-tuning SAM on specific limited-scale medical datasets. While these methods have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image segmentation tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2) Different prompt modes play important roles in different segmentation tasks when migrating SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the medical field. As shown in Figure 2 (c), a relatively accurate polyp mask can be obtained by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using the bounding box prompt. In contrast, the mask quality is poor when clicking on a foreground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: point (column d). With an increasing number of clicks, the segmentation result gradually improves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and even surpasses the performance of the bounding box prompt (e.g., liver segmentation). When

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmenting myocardium, using the bounding box prompt may include uninterested regions in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: result, while the point prompt allows us to gradually acquire the desired mask. Therefore, this paper

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aims to fine-tune three prompt modes (point, bounding box, and mask) to meet the requirements

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of different scenarios in medical image segmentation tasks. According to Table 1, our approach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: involves a more comprehensive fine-tuning compared to other methods, which means our method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: possesses a broader range of prompt segmentation capabilities in the medical image domain.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3) Adapters have been proven to be an effective strategy for fine-tuning large-scale models [21, 43].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: They do not require retraining the entire model, ensuring that the original knowledge is not forgotten.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This enables an existing model to excel in both new and the original tasks. Due to the parameter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sharing property of adapters, they facilitate transfer learning between different tasks. Therefore, this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paper applies Adapter to the encoder of SAM to learn domain-specific information in the field of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical imaging. Additionally, the adapter layer is a plug-and-play component that allows us to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: choose whether to keep or remove it during the testing process, according to our specific needs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • How to evaluate the performance of SAM-Med2D?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To comprehensively evaluate the performance of SAM-Med2D in the medical imaging domain,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we assessed its capabilities from multiple perspectives. We focused on the following aspects: 1)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Data diversity: We evaluated SAM-Med2D on various imaging modalities such as CT, MR, X-ray,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different organs, and multiple pathological conditions like tumors, inflammations, etc., to ensure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its ability to segment different types of medical images. 2) Fine-tuning strategy: We compare

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the default fine-tuning strategy of SAM-Med2D with other alternative strategies, e.g., different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model configurations, to demonstrate SAM-Med2D's success in the medical imaging domain. 3)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Generalization ability: We evaluated the robustness of SAM-Med2D using 9 MICCAI2023 datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to ensure its accurate segmentation in unseen medical image environments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Through comprehensive evaluation, we found that SAM-Med2D possesses the following capabilities:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) Medical expertise: Compared to SAM, SAM-Med2D demonstrates superior performance in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: handling complex organ structures, lesions, and cases with unclear boundaries. This means that SAM-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Med2D can accurately identify and segment challenging areas in medical images, thus providing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more precise diagnostic and treatment support. 2) Broad segmentation capabilities: SAM-Med2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: demonstrates a broad segmentation capability across various prompt modes, enabling it to fulfill

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation tasks in different scenarios. This implies that doctors and medical imaging professionals

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can utilize SAM-Med2D to perform more precise and accurate segmentation operations, thereby

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhancing the efficiency and reliability of medical image analysis results. 3) Generalization ability:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM-Med2D demonstrates strong generalization ability, allowing direct application to unseen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image data and producing good segmentation results.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Large-scale Vision Models (LVM). Inspired by large language models such as ChatGPT and GPT-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 44, researchers have developed similar LVM including [7, 8, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26]. These models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exhibit outstanding zero-shot and few-shot generalization capabilities, enabling rapid adaptation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and extension to target tasks or domains through pre-training and fine-tuning paradigms. Among

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: them, CLIP [23] provides a unified vision and language model that can be utilized for various tasks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: including classification, detection, and visual question answering. Through extensive pre-training on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: text and image pairs, this model has achieved impressive results in multiple benchmark tests. DALL.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: E [25] is a variant of the Large-Scale Transformer model, GPT-3, trained to generate images based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on textual descriptions. Recently, SAM [8] pre-trained on 1B masks has become a general-purpose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: LVM for image segmentation. It demonstrates powerful zero-shot capabilities, allowing interactive or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: automatic segmentation of any object. In contrast, SegGPT [7] unifies different segmentation tasks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into a single contextual learning framework by transforming diverse segmentation data into images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a standardized format. Furthermore, SEEM [26] proposes a universal interface that employs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multi-modal prompts to simultaneously segment all contents in images or videos and identify object

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: categories. However, these LVMs have not been explicitly optimized for the field of Medical Image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Analysis (MIA).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fine-tuned SAM in Medical Image Analysis. SAM provides an excellent framework for inter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: active segmentation, making it a benchmark model for prompt-based medical image segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, due to significant domain differences between natural images and medical images, SAM's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance significantly declines when applied to medical images [16, 17, 18, 20, 21]. Current

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: research primarily focuses on fine-tuning SAM for specific medical segmentation datasets. Deng

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. [16] proposed a multi-box prompt triggering uncertainty estimation for SAM, achieving sig-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nificant improvements in retinal image segmentation. Zhang et al. [17] applied a low-rank-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine-tuning strategy to the SAM encoder while simultaneously fine-tuning the decoder for abdominal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation tasks. Hu et al. [18] abandoned the original prompt encoder of SAM and constructed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different types of prediction heads for fine-tuning to accomplish automated cardiac segmentation. Ma

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. [20] collected 11 different modalities of medical image data and fine-tuned the mask decoder of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM on over 1M masks while preserving the original box prompt. In contrast to the aforementioned

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: studies, Wu et al. [21] proposed the MSA, which integrates medical-specific domain knowledge into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM using a simple adapter technique and validated it on 19 medical image segmentation tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These studies demonstrate that fine-tuning or adapter techniques can improve SAM's performance in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image segmentation. Unlike the aforementioned methods that only provide bounding box or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: point prompt, we adapt SAM to medical image segmentation by using more comprehensive prompts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4https://openai.com/research/gpt-4

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (i.e., bounding box, points, and mask). In addition, we comprehensively analyze the performance and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenges of our method in medical image segmentation by considering different imaging modalities,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: anatomical structures, and organs in medical images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Zero-shot evaluation of SAM in medical imaging. Recent studies have reported the zero-shot per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formance of SAM in medical image segmentation. Deng et al. [27] investigated SAM's segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capabilities on tumor and tissue tasks under different prompt conditions, and the experimental results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: show that SAM performs better only on segmenting large connected objects. Hu et al. [28] evaluated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the impact of point prompts on SAM's performance in multi-phase liver tumor segmentation in CT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volumes. The results demonstrated that SAM's performance improved as the number of point prompts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increased. Zhou et al. [12] tested SAM's performance in colonoscopy polyp segmentation without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompts, and the results indicated significant room for improvement when applying SAM to polyp

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation tasks. Cheng et al. [29] extensively evaluated the following models on 12 open-source

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image datasets: promptless models, models with 1, 3, and 10-point prompts, and models with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: box prompts with 5 different jitter levels. The performance of SAM was generally lower compared

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to state-of-the-art results. Similarly, Huang et al. [15] evaluated the zero-shot performance of SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on 52 public datasets using three different prompts, and the evaluation results consistently showed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unsatisfactory performance of SAM across various medical image segmentation tasks. We believe

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that analyzing SAM's performance on large-scale medical image datasets is crucial. This can help

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the community gain a better understanding of the factors influencing the model's ability to perceive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical objects. These factors can contribute to the improved development of general medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation methods. Therefore, this study provides a comprehensive evaluation of SAM-Med2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from multiple perspectives.

layout_dets.text: 3 Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1 Incorporation of Medical Knowledge into SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recent research has reaffirmed the pivotal role of training data volume in the learning capacity of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large models [7, 8, 23]. By learning from larger-scale data, models can acquire richer domain-specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: knowledge and adapt better to various application scenarios. Though trained on over 1B masks,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM achieves suboptimal performance in the realm of medical image analysis due to the significant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain gap between natural images and medical data. To address this gap, we have collected and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curated the largest medical image segmentation dataset to date. This dataset is composed of numerous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: public and private datasets, ensuring comprehensive coverage and diversity. Figure 3 (b) illustrates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the dataset's 10 different imaging modalities and their corresponding data proportions. To enhance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: visual presentation, we have used logarithmic scaling to visualize the differences in quantity. Based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on anatomical structures and the presence of lesions, we categorized the dataset into head and neck,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thorax, abdomen, pelvic, and lesions (Figure 3 (c)). Additionally, we curated and consolidated 31

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: main organs from the 271 labels in these datasets, as depicted in Figure 3 (a). This covers almost all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object types in the currently available public datasets, addressing the deficiency of SAM in medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain knowledge.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For the effective application of SAM to medical image segmentation, we preprocessed the dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from multiple angles. Firstly, for 3D datasets, we normalized the intensity values of each volume

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the range [0, 255] and extracted all slice images and their corresponding masks along the x, y,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and z axes. In the extraction process, slice images with the shortest edge less than half the length

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the longest edge were discarded to prevent target areas from becoming extremely blurry when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adjusting for images with large aspect ratios. For 2D datasets, we only checked whether pixel values

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were within the range [0, 255], and all processed images were saved in PNG format to maintain data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loading consistency. Secondly, when a mask contained multiple classes, we generated multiple masks,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each containing only one class (similar to sam1B [8]). We also split masks with multiple connected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: components (for example, left and right lungs) into multiple masks with single connected components.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: If multiple organs were present and only contained one connected component, we retained the mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to increase data diversity. Lastly, we excluded masks where the target area constituted less than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the total image, meaning that when an image is resized to 256×256, its target

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: area must exceed 100 pixels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Following these procedures, we obtained approximately 4.6M images and 19.7M masks. We randomly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: split 80% data for training and 20% for testing based on image indices. The resulting training set

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: included roughly 3.67M images and 15.8M masks, while the test set contained 0.92M images and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.9M masks. We also introduced 9 MICCAI2023 datasets (comprising about 0.52M images and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.31M masks) that served solely to validate the model's generalization ability. We believe that with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more comprehensive and diverse set of training data, SAM will better adapt to the complexities and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nuances of the medical imaging field, providing more accurate and reliable support for applications

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in healthcare. This will also usher in new opportunities and challenges for research and development

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the field of medical image segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 4: The pipeline of SAM-Med2D. We freeze the image encoder and incorporate learnable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adapter layers in each Transformer block to acquire domain-specific knowledge in the medical field.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We fine-tune the prompt encoder using point, Bbox, and mask information, while updating the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters of the mask decoder through interactive training.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2 Transition from SAM to SAM-Med2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Before introducing SAM-Med2D, let us briefly review the SAM architecture. SAM consists of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: three main components: a large-scale image encoder, a prompt encoder, and a lightweight mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder. This framework allows for different masks to be generated for the same image based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on different prompts. The image encoder utilizes a pre-trained Visual Transformer (ViT) [22] to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process high-resolution inputs and outputs feature maps at a 1/16 scale of the original image. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompt encoder includes sparse prompts and dense prompts, mapping points, bounding boxes, or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: text to 256-dimensional vectors and applying convolutional down-sampling to dense prompts with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: GELU activation function at each level. The mask decoder receives embedded information from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both encoders, and updates the image embeddings and prompt embeddings through a cross-attention

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanism. In this work, we fine-tune SAM to create SAM-Med2D, which effectively extends the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: framework to the domain of medical images. We will now discuss each component of SAM-Med2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the fine-tuning strategies in detail.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. Adapting Image Encoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As the most parameter-heavy part of SAM, globally updating the image encoder during fine-tuning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: incurs significant computational costs. To incorporate medical domain knowledge into the image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoder at a lower cost, we introduce Adapter technology. Specifically, we freeze all parameters of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the original image encoder during fine-tuning and deploy an adapter for each Transformer block, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in Figure 4. We adapt the image encoder along both channel and spatial dimensions. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the channel dimension, we first compress the resolution of the input feature map to C×1×1 using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: global average pooling. Then, we employ a linear layer to compress the channel embeddings and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: another linear layer to restore them, with a compression ratio of 0.25. Finally, we obtain the weights

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the channel dimension through a sigmoid function and multiply them with the input feature map

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as the input for the next level. For the spatial dimension, we downsample the spatial resolution of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feature map by a factor of two using a convolutional layer and restore the spatial resolution using a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transposed convolution, maintaining the same number of channels as the input. A skip connection is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: added after each adapter layer.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: B. Prompt Encoder and Mask Decoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The prompt encoder in SAM supports four types of prompts: point, bounding box, mask, and text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompts. Due to the lack of large-scale pre-trained models for medical image-text alignment, the use

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of text prompts is limited. Therefore, we only consider the remaining three prompt modes for fine-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tuning. Compared to previous methods that fine-tune a single prompt only [20, 21], we retain the full

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: functionality of prompts and enhance their applicability in the medical imaging domain. Specifically,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM-Med2D utilizes both sparse prompts (point and bounding box) and dense prompts (mask)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: simultaneously. For sparse prompts, each point is represented as a vector embedding of its positional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoding along with the sum of two learned embeddings indicating its foreground or background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: position. Each bounding box uses the positional encoding of its top-left and bottom-right corners,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: along with learned embeddings representing "top-left" and "bottom-right" as vector embeddings. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dense prompts, we use the low-resolution feature map generated after the first iteration of the model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as the mask prompt, applying two convolutional embeddings that reduce the scale of the input mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by a factor of 4 with output channels of 1/4 and 1/16 of the original input. Finally, a 1×1 convolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is used to map the channel dimension to 256.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We did not make any changes to the mask decoder structure and kept updating its parameters during

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training. To make the model ambiguity-aware, each prompt predicts multiple masks simultaneously

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (defaulting to three). During backpropagation, we choose the predicted mask with the highest

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Intersection over Union (IoU) score relative to the ground truth to calculate the loss, propagating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gradients accordingly. We map the low-resolution feature map generated from the previous iteration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the range of [0, 1] as the dense prompt for the current iteration. During the actual training process,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we observed that even with only sparse prompts, the model can quickly converge, which diminishes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the impact of dense prompts. Therefore, we adopt the training strategy of SAM, where in the last

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: iteration and one random intermediate iteration, we only provide dense prompts to encourage the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model to benefit from the provided masks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: C. Fine-tuning Strategy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Similar to SAM and other interactive segmentation methods [30], we train SAM-Med2D by simulating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interactive segmentation. For each batch of data, we train the model for 9 iterations. In the first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: iteration, we randomly select a foreground point or bounding box as the sparse prompt with equal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: probabilities. The foreground point is sampled from the ground truth, and the bounding box is the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maximum enclosing rectangle of the ground truth, with each coordinate offset by a maximum of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: five pixels. It is worth noting that except for the first iteration, where the parameters of the Adapter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer, prompt encoder, and mask decoder are updated simultaneously, subsequent iterations only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: update the parameters of the mask decoder. Starting from the second iteration, we randomly select

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1, 3, 5, or 9 points from the error region between the previous mask predictions and the ground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: truth as subsequent sparse prompts, allowing users to perform single-point or multi-point interactive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation. SAM-Med2D aims to improve the segmentation of medical images by adapting the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM framework specifically for the medical imaging domain. It incorporates adapter technology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extends the functionality of prompts, and uses a fine-tuning strategy based on simulated interactive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.3 Evaluate SAM-Med2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Comprehensive performance evaluation is crucial for the research community to gain a deeper

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: understanding of the factors influencing the algorithm's ability to perceive medical objects, thereby

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improving methods and enhancing their effectiveness in practical applications. However, previous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluations [11, 12, 13, 15] have been limited by the scarcity of data and the lack of a benchmark

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for general medical image segmentation methods, resulting in evaluations confined to small-scale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets and limited categories, failing to fully reveal the strengths and applicability of algorithms.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To address this research gap, we will conduct a comprehensive and multidimensional evaluation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM-Med2D, providing a benchmark for interactive segmentation methods for future researchers.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In terms of models, we take SAM as the baseline model and select two intuitive prompt modes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Bbox and Points, from its interaction methods to evaluate SAM-Med2D. This choice was made

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: because Bbox and points are commonly used interaction modes and can serve as simple and efficient

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotation methods. By evaluating the performance of SAM-Med2D under these two interaction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modes, we can delve into their advantages and limitations in medical image segmentation tasks. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Bbox interaction mode guides the algorithm to perform segmentation by bounding the target with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: box, which is intuitive and easy to understand. It provides rough positional and shape information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the target, thereby guiding the algorithm to perform more accurate segmentation. However, in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some cases, accurately enclosing the target with a Bbox may be challenging, especially for complex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shaped targets, targets with blurred edges, or overlapping objects. This may result in inaccuracies in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation results and instances of missed segmentation. On the other hand, the points interaction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mode guides the algorithm to perform segmentation by marking key points or regions of the target.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This mode can provide more precise segmentation guidance, particularly for targets with complex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shapes or local details. These evaluations will help us gain a deeper understanding of the strengths

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and limitations of different interaction modes in medical image segmentation, thereby inspiring

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: researchers to design and develop more flexible and efficient interaction patterns.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In terms of data, we will evaluate the performance of SAM-Med2D on 10 different modalities of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical images, including MRI, CT, ultrasound, and more. This comprehensive evaluation will allow

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: us to understand the strengths and challenges of SAM-Med2D under specific modalities and reveal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its potential application capabilities in multimodal images. Different medical image modalities have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distinct characteristics and sources of noise, so evaluating SAM-Med2D's performance on these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modalities will provide a more comprehensive understanding of its applicability and robustness.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Furthermore, considering that different anatomical structures and organs have unique morphologies,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: features, and variation patterns, we conducted evaluations of SAM-Med2D on four anatomical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures and 31 major organs. Such evaluations help us gain in-depth insights into the performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differences of SAM-Med2D in different scenarios and enable targeted improvements to address chal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lenges specific to certain structures and organs. Lastly, we place great emphasis on the generalization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ability of SAM-Med2D and therefore tested it on 9 MICCAI 2023 datasets. These datasets represent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical images collected from different sources, institutions, or devices, providing diversity. By

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluating SAM-Med2D on these datasets, we can verify its ability to generalize to new data. This is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crucial in validating the applicability of our method to a wide range of clinical scenarios and data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sources.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Through the above comprehensive evaluation, we will be able to provide in-depth insights into the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance and applicability of SAM-Med2D, serving as a valuable reference and benchmark

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for future researchers and developers. These evaluation results will have a positive impact on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: development of medical image segmentation, promoting the design and application of more accurate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and efficient methods.

layout_dets.text: 4 Experiments and Evaluation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.1 Implementation Details

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our method is implemented in PyTorch and trained on 8 NVIDIA Tesla A100 GPUs, each with 80GB

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: memory. Considering the memory constraints, we only fine-tune the base model of SAM (SAM-B)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in this work. We use the Adam optimizer with an initial learning rate of 1e-4 and train for a total

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 12 epochs, with the learning rate divided by 2 at the 7th and 10th epochs. During training, all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images are resized to a resolution of 256x256. Our resizing strategy involves padding the edges with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: zeros for images with both width and height smaller than 256, while using bilinear interpolation to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resize images in other cases. For each image, we randomly select 5 corresponding masks. If there are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fewer masks available, we randomly duplicate samples. To make full use of GPU memory, each GPU

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processes 50 images along with their corresponding 250 masks. The loss function supervising the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask predictions is a linear combination of focal loss [31] and dice loss [32], with a ratio of 20:1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Additionally, the mean squared error loss between the intersection over union (IoU) prediction and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the predicted mask with ground truth mask is used for training. We use the Dice score to evaluate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation results.

layout_dets.text: 4.2 Quantitative Evaluation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. Overall Performance. Table 2 presents the overall performance results of SAM, FT-SAM (only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine-tune the mask decoder), and our SAM-Med2D on test set. We found that in the bounding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: box prompt (Bbox prompt) mode, FT-SAM achieved an 11.93% improvement in Dice score over

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM, while our SAM-Med2D achieved a more significant performance boost, with Dice scores

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 79.30% (i.e., 17.67% boost). This indicates that fine-tuning on a large-scale dataset can lead to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: better transferability in the target domain. We also simulated interactive segmentation in the point

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompt mode. In this mode, we randomly sampled a point from the foreground as the first prompt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: point, and subsequent prompt points were randomly selected within the error region between the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation result and the ground truth. Additionally, the low-resolution mask generated in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: previous iteration was used as the mask prompt, along with the previous prompt points, as input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the model. Experimental results showed that SAM performed poorly when using a single point

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompt, even with a resolution of 1024×1024, exhibiting a 23.23% lower Dice score compared to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FT-SAM. As the number of prompt points increased, the performance of different models significantly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improved, with the fine-tuned approach even surpassing the Bbox prompt mode. This demonstrates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the feasibility and effectiveness of using point-based interactive segmentation in medical images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Furthermore, the overall segmentation performance of SAM at a resolution of 1024×1024 was inferior

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to that of the fine-tuned approach. This indicates that the fine-tuned model learned specific knowledge

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the medical domain, and fine-tuning with low cost is an effective and feasible method to reduce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain differences.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: B. Performance Evaluation on Anatomical Structures. As shown in Figure 5 (a), we evaluated the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation performance of different models and resolutions on the head and neck (H&N), thorax

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Tx), abdomen (Abd), pelvis (Pl), and other regions. The "other regions" includes lesions and cases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outside the aforementioned four anatomical structures. Our main focus was on the segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance of the models using Bbox prompt and 1 point prompt (1 pt prompt).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We observed that when using the Bbox prompt, SAM (at 1024 ×1024 resolution) outperformed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FT-SAM in the Tx, Abd, and other regions. However, it showed poorer performance in the H&N

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: region. This can be attributed to the relatively smaller size of lesions or organs in the H&N area, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: well as the presence of less clear boundaries, making it challenging for the model to adapt to this type

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5 Discussion and Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this study, we obtain SAM-Med2D by fine-tuning a SAM on a large-scale medical image dataset,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is able to significantly improve various medical image segmentation tasks. We employed two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explicit prompts strategies to generate masks for quantitative and qualitative comparisons. At an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: equal resolution, only the fine-tuned mask decoder (FT-SAM) achieved an improvement of 11.93%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the Bbox prompt mode, while the fully fine-tuned SAM-Med2D achieved a 17.67% improvement.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Surprisingly, our approach demonstrated overwhelming superiority in the 1 pt prompt (18.94% vs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 70.01%). Furthermore, SAM-Med2D exhibited excellent generalization capabilities in both prompt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modes, indicating its practical value in the medical field.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the model from different dimensions of the data. From

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an anatomical perspective, at a resolution of 1024×1024, SAM had advantages over FT-SAM in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the chest, abdomen, and other regions, SAM-Med2D outperformed all other methods in overall

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation performance. Regarding different modalities, SAM demonstrated good generalization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: when the target modality data resembled natural image attributes. We compared the two fine-tuning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods on more than 30 major organs, and our SAM-Med2D achieved better results on 24 organs,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a maximum improvement of 6.95% compared to FT-SAM. Additionally, our generalization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experiments on 9 publicly available datasets demonstrated strong domain transferability of models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pretrained on large-scale datasets. While the Bbox prompt always outperformed the 1 pt prompt,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adding more points significantly improved the segmentation results, surpassing even the Bbox mode.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: When using the point prompt mode, SAM-Med2D was able to generate the desired masks more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quickly, even outperforming other methods using the Bbox prompt mode.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, further optimization is required for more robust medical image segmentation in the future.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: From the qualitative segmentation results, for complex shapes/boundaries, small size or low contrast

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: objects, there is still room for improvement in the segmentation results produced by different prompt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modes. Establishing relevant optimization strategies in the future may enhance the segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results, such as setting window width for different organs and designing boundary loss for interactive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation. In addition to the prompt strategies used in this paper, natural language can serve as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: another common form of user interaction in medical image segmentation, but currently, there is a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lack of relevant datasets. This is a direction we actively pursue, aiming to equip SAM-Med2D with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: natural language understanding capabilities in the medical domain to meet diverse user needs. While

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we have trained SAM-Med2D on over 19.7M masks, there is still a gap compared to the training data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and resolution of SAM. This results in SAM-Med2D being effective in handling common organs or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lesions but lacking the "everything" capability in the medical domain. We plan to generate a larger

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quantity and wider variety of high-quality masks through data engines, enabling SAM-Med2D to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: truly segment all types of medical images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In summary, this work fine-tuned the SAM on a large-scale medical image dataset to adapt it to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the medical image domain. SAM-Med2D achieved satisfactory performance improvements and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generalization capabilities. Our code and pre-trained models will be made available for researchers,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and we hope this work benefits researchers in the field of medical computer vision, providing insights

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and opportunities for future research and improvements.
